notes_for_review: An LLM writes a numerical update program (essentially regularized least squares or L-BFGS over a small permitted parameter set) that is rerun on accumulating experimental feedback; the LLM does not choose weight values directly. The Adam baseline shares data and parameters, but Adam fits from zero correction with a fixed learning rate, so the gap may reflect closed-form ridge fitting versus a tuned-light optimizer rather than LLM insight. The four prediction-task results come from one execution seed and report no variance; no limitations section is given. The paper is short (5 pages) and not peer reviewed. The source PDF is two-column with interleaved extraction, so quotes are short single-column fragments.
